title: Drishyam 3 — Mohanlal's Franchise Finale Lands with ₹100 Crore Bet and a Global Premiere
excerpt: PEN Studios' record-breaking investment in the Malayalam thriller's conclusion signals a permanent power shift in Indian cinema, with 500+ screens worldwide and $1M+ in international pre-sales.
body:
Georgekutty is back. And this time, the stakes aren't just cinematic — they're financial.

**Drishyam 3**, the grand finale of Jeethu Joseph's beloved thriller franchise, releases on May 21 (Mohanlal's 66th birthday, because of course it does), and it arrives carrying the weight of a ₹100 crore investment from PEN Studios — the single biggest bet ever placed on a Malayalam film.

Let that number breathe for a second. One hundred crore rupees. On a Malayalam-language movie. In 2026. If you needed proof that South Indian cinema has permanently rewritten Bollywood's monopoly on big-budget filmmaking, here it is, wrapped in a murder mystery.

## The Numbers Don't Lie

The pre-release buzz is staggering. Domestic pre-sales have already crossed ₹15 crore. International pre-sales? Over $1 million — and climbing. Advance booking in Kerala alone topped ₹4 crore gross, while worldwide advance sales have crossed ₹10 crore.

The film is rolling out on **500+ screens outside Kerala**, a distribution footprint that would've been unthinkable for a Malayalam film even three years ago. Industry trackers expect a **₹35 crore+ global opening**, which would surpass the record set by *Empuraan* earlier this year.

For context: **Drishyam 2** (2021) was already a phenomenon, the rare sequel that matched its predecessor. Now the trilogy closer arrives with expectations that make those numbers look quaint.

## Two Films, One Story

Here's an unusual wrinkle that NRI audiences should know about: **Drishyam 3 exists as two different films.** The Malayalam original and the Hindi version aren't just dubbed copies — they're **different cuts**, each tailored to its audience. Mohanlal and Meena lead the Malayalam version; the Hindi adaptation gets its own treatment.

This dual-version strategy is fascinating. It acknowledges what the industry has learned the hard way: dubbing doesn't cut it anymore. North Indian audiences want a version that speaks to them natively, not a translation. South Indian audiences want their star, their language, their rhythm. PEN Studios is betting ₹100 crore that both can coexist.

## The OTT Wildcard

Now, here's where it gets spicy for diaspora viewers. **Amazon Prime Video** holds the OTT rights — but there's a legal storm brewing. A dispute between Amazon and Aashirvad Cinemas (Mohanlal's production house) over the digital deal has landed in the Delhi High Court. The court granted interim relief, but the streaming timeline remains uncertain.

What does this mean for you, sitting in Houston or Brampton or Sydney? **It means the theater is your best bet.** With 500+ screens internationally and the OTT situation unresolved, Drishyam 3 is essentially *forcing* a theatrical experience — and honestly, for a film this big, that might be exactly how it should be watched.

## Why Georgekutty Still Matters

The Drishyam franchise has always been more than a thriller. It's a story about an ordinary man — no wealth, no connections, no English-medium education — who outsmarts the system through sheer intelligence and desperate love for his family. For the Indian diaspora, there's something deeply resonant about that. The immigrant experience, after all, is its own kind of survival story.

Principal photography ran from September to December 2025, with Jeethu Joseph reportedly crafting a conclusion that honors both films while delivering genuine surprises. Early whispers from test screenings suggest emotional gut-punches that rival the first film's legendary climax.

## The Bigger Picture

Drishyam 3 isn't just a movie release. It's a statement. When a Malayalam film commands ₹100 crore in investment, gets 500+ screens worldwide, and triggers legal battles over its OTT rights, the power dynamics of Indian cinema have officially, permanently shifted.

The era when South Indian films needed Bollywood validation is over. Mohanlal's Georgekutty proved that five years ago. Now he's back to remind everyone — one last time.

*Drishyam 3 releases globally on May 21, 2026. Check your local listings for showtimes — with 500+ screens outside Kerala, there's likely a screening near you.*
